newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australia retail trade, Q3 stocks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-INSTANT VIEW-Australia retail trade, Q3 stocks.

text.p: Australian retail sales rose 1.4 percent in October after a 3.7 percent fall in September, according to data released by the Australian Bureau of Statistics. Forecasts had centred on a 2.0 percent rise.
The ABS also said building approvals for October rose 12.8 percent against an expected 5.0 percent increase and after an 8.6 percent fall in the previous month.
The Bureau also said that third quarter stocks rose 2.3 percent compared with forecasts for a 0.55 percent rise.
A selection of immediate reactions to the data follows:
CRAIG JAMES, SENIOR ECONOMIST, COLONIAL STATE BANK:

"It is a bit of a mixed picture, but the retail sales number really deserves significant focus. Retail sales is now falling in trend terms, and really even in the recession in the early 1990s we didn't see retail sales falling, so it does suggest a very soft consumer picture. In terms of building approvals it is the first strong figure that we have had for some time, and in trend terms building approvals are now rising, so it does give hope for the housing sector running forward."
